audit.whatIsWrong: Every row of the level chart contradicts its own why text and the packet. The chart renders Kennen / Skill x5 / Kennen while whys[] describe even, Kennen, Kennen, Urgot, Urgot, Kennen, Urgot — which is exactly the packet levelChart.
audit.why: The prose layer already got this lane right: Kennen out-ranges at 2-3, Urgot takes over at 4-5 with the R threat, Kennen reasserts at 6 when Maelstrom plus Lightning Rush are both up, and Urgot wins after first item. Only the side tokens were never updated, so a paying user reads 'Skill' on rows the text calls a Kennen lane.
audit.corrected: All seven rows proposed as matched full+content pairs to the packet chart: Skill / Kennen / Kennen / Urgot / Urgot / Kennen / Urgot, with ratings realigned and four phase whys rewritten to say the real reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 and first-item spikes were described without a single cooldown number, and phases[5].why claimed a Black Cleaver Urgot spike on a row the data gives to Kennen.
audit.why: Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120s at every rank and Lightning Rush is 10s at rank 1 falling to 6s. The danger window is precisely when both are up; after Maelstrom is spent Urgot has two full minutes of free lane.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why rewritten to the Maelstrom-plus-Lightning-Rush window; breakdown.cooldowns given the real 120s and 10s figures.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mark of the Storm's three-hit stun is named nowhere in the interaction fields, and dosFull[2] says 'Build MR' with a body text about wasting Lightning Rush. Electrical Surge's on-hit component is also absent.
audit.why: The decisive early interaction is that Kennen's Q-auto weave applies marks and the third one stuns — that is what turns his poke into a kill. And his damage is magic on-hit scaling with attack speed via Electrical Surge, so armour reads the trade wrong; MR is the correct answer, which is what the page tells you to build without ever saying why. Per the mirror, Corrosive Charge is Q (the 800-range slow) and Disdain is E (the 475-range shielded charge-flip) — the shield eats his burst, so bait it before you commit R.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d now states the on-hit/attack-speed scaling; dontsFull[1].d now states the third-mark stun; phases[2].why names the Q-auto mark chain.

edits.before: E or W second depending on kill pressure. A landed E-flip into W spray already wins most level-2 exchanges outright.
edits.after: Thundering Shuriken reaches 950 to your Q's 800 — he pokes for free at level 2, so take W and farm the wave, not him.

edits.before: Full legs rotation online — this is your lane now. Walk Kennen down with W whenever Lightning Rush is on cooldown.
edits.after: He zones your CS and stacks Mark of the Storm off Q-auto weaves. Three marks is a stun, so break the chain and step out.

edits.before: Black Cleaver stacks instantly with W — your shred turns even tanky answers soft. Shove and force Kennen to trade into the spike.
edits.after: Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120s, but with Lightning Rush also up his all-in reasserts — give nothing while both are available.

edits.before: - Kennen Lightning Rush: matchup-defining — His escape/engage. Flip it with your E. Track it before every engage. - Kennen Slicing Maelstrom: A storm around him that repeatedly damages + stuns via marks. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Kennen Lightning Rush: 10s at rank 1 falling to 6s — his escape and his engage, so commit only while it is down. - Kennen Slicing Maelstrom: a flat 120s storm that re-marks and stuns through the fight. Bait it, then take the lane.

edits.before: His escape/engage. Flip it with your E. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His escape and his engage, 10s at rank 1. Only commit once it is down or baited.

edits.before: Kennen wastes Lightning Rush — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: His W is magic on-hit that scales with attack speed — MR beats armour here.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Mark of the Storm stuns on the third application — break the Q-auto chain.
